instruction: How do the -p publish variants work, and how do I bind localhost only?
output: `-p 8080:80` binds all interfaces; `127.0.0.1:8080:80` binds loopback only (do this for dev databases/admin UIs so LAN strangers cannot reach them); `-p 8080` picks a random host port for the container's 80; `-P` publishes all EXPOSEd ports randomly. Check with `docker port web`. Never publish management ports (2375, DBs) on 0.0.0.0 in production.

instruction: Should I use -v or --mount, and what does the long syntax give?
output: Prefer `--mount type=volume,src=data,dst=/data,readonly` — it is explicit, fails on typos (no auto-created dirs), and supports tmpfs options and consistency flags. `-v` is shorter for interactive use but silently creates host dirs on typo. Rule: `--mount` in scripts/compose files, `-v` at the terminal. Both cannot be mixed on one path.

instruction: Why does Chrome or Postgres crash in containers with shm errors?
output: Docker defaults /dev/shm to 64MB, too small for Chromium renderers and large Postgres sorts. Raise it with `docker run --shm-size 2g` (Compose: `shm_size: 2g`). Symptoms are cryptic tab crashes and `could not resize shared memory segment` errors — always check shm before blaming the app.

instruction: Which kernel knobs matter per container: sysctl, pids-limit, oom-score?
output: Set `net.core.somaxconn=1024` for high-connection proxies/Redis via `--sysctl` (namespaced ones only; host-wide needs daemon config). Contain fork bombs with `--pids-limit 256`. Tune OOM preference with `--oom-score-adj -500` for critical sidecars — and never `--oom-kill-disable` unless you accept a frozen host instead of a killed container.

instruction: COPY --chown, ADD vs COPY, and verifying remote ADDs?
output: Prefer `COPY --chown=app:app --chmod=755 src/ /app/` over extra RUN chown layers. Use ADD only for its two extras: tar auto-extract and remote URL fetch — and verify fetches with `ADD --checksum=sha256:<hex> https://... /tmp/x`. Everything else should be COPY: predictable, cacheable, no magic.

instruction: How do I use secrets and SSH in builds without leaking?
output: Build secrets never persist in layers, unlike ARG: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc cat /run/secrets/npmrc` with `docker build --secret id=npmrc,src=.npmrc .`. For private repos forward the agent: `RUN --mount=type=ssh git clone git@github.com:org/repo.git` with `docker build --ssh default .`. Both require BuildKit and leave zero trace in history.

instruction: How do .dockerignore negations and heredoc RUN blocks work?
output:
Exclude broadly then re-include: `*.log` plus `!keep/important.log` (last match wins, and you cannot re-include files under an excluded directory). For multi-line scripts use heredocs instead of chained && with backslashes:
```dockerfile
RUN <<EOF
set -e
apt-get update
apt-get install -y curl
EOF
```
Heredocs fail visibly per line and read like real scripts.

instruction: What does COPY --link do for rebuild speed?
output: `COPY --link` creates each layer independently of its parent, so changing an early COPY no longer invalidates everything below it — rebuilds stay fast in big Dockerfiles. Requires BuildKit. Combine with multi-stage + dependency-first ordering and your worst-case rebuild approaches your best case.

instruction: How do I debug production images without shipping a shell?
output: Add a debug stage sharing the build: `FROM base AS debug` installing busybox/strace, while prod stays distroless — build with `--target debug` only when troubleshooting. Or use distroless `:debug` variants bundling busybox. Never let the debug stage reach production registries: tag it `-debug` and gate promotion on exact prod tags.

instruction: docker vs docker-container build drivers — why does it matter?
output: The default `docker` driver is fast but cannot do multi-arch, registry cache export, or attestations — create a real builder: `docker buildx create --driver docker-container --use`. Manage disk with `docker buildx du` and `docker buildx prune`. Mysterious missing features in CI are almost always the wrong driver, not the wrong flags.

instruction: How do registry and GHA cache backends work for builds?
output: Share layers across machines with `--cache-to type=registry,ref=user/app:cache --cache-from type=registry,ref=user/app:cache`, or `--cache-to type=inline` (works with plain push, weaker). In GitHub Actions use `type=gha` via docker/build-push-action `cache-from/to`. Cache misses silently fall back to full builds — watch build times to confirm hits.

instruction: What is buildx bake and when do I need it?
output: Bake builds many targets from an HCL file instead of long shell loops: `docker buildx bake -f docker-bake.hcl release` with targets, groups, matrix (arch × variant) and shared args in one place. Reach for it when you build >2 images or matrix across arches — below that, plain buildx commands stay readable.

instruction: How do Docker Hub rate limits bite CI, and how do I mirror?
output: Anonymous pulls are capped (100/6h per IP) — shared CI NAT gateways hit `toomanyrequests` fast. Fix: `docker login` in CI (200 pulls/6h), or run a pull-through cache (`registry:2` with `proxy.remoteurl`) and set `registry-mirrors` in daemon.json. Always mirror or authenticate before blaming flaky pulls.

instruction: How do I manage registries without the Docker daemon (crane/regctl/oras)?
output: `crane ls user/app`, `crane digest`, `crane copy src dst` manipulate registries over HTTPS with no daemon — ideal in CI. `regctl image copy` handles cross-registry sync; `oras push/pull` stores arbitrary artifacts (SBOMs, policies) in OCI registries. These tools turn registry chores into one-liners instead of pull-tag-push cycles.

instruction: How do I debug container DNS (127.0.0.11)?
output: Containers use the embedded DNS at 127.0.0.11 — test from inside with `nslookup web` or `getent hosts db`. Override per container with `--dns 8.8.8.8 --dns-search example.com`, daemon-wide in daemon.json `dns` key. If names resolve on host but not in containers, suspect corporate VPN DNS interception or a custom daemon dns that shadows the embedded server.

instruction: VPN up and container networking broke — MTU?
output: Classic symptom: small requests work, large transfers hang. VPNs shrink usable MTU below Docker's 1500 default — set daemon.json `"mtu": 1450` (or per network `docker network create -o com.docker.network.driver.mtu=1450 net`) and recreate containers. Diagnose with `ping -M do -s 1472 target` shrinking until replies pass, then set MTU slightly below.

instruction: How does a container reach services on the host?
output: From containers use `host.docker.internal` (Desktop; on Linux add `--add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway` or Compose `extra_hosts`). It resolves to the host gateway, not localhost — `localhost` inside a container is the container itself. For fixed IPs, inspect the bridge gateway (`docker network inspect bridge -f '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'`). Never hardcode another container's bridge IP.

instruction: Can I attach networks or aliases to a running container?
output: Yes: `docker network connect --alias api-v2 appnet web` adds a live container to another network with an extra DNS name; `docker network disconnect appnet web` removes it. Aliases are per-network, so one container answers different names on different nets. For Swarm overlay debugging, create the network `--attachable` first or standalone containers cannot join it.

instruction: Why are my Compose resource limits ignored?
output: `deploy.resources` only applies to Swarm stacks — plain `docker compose` silently ignores it. For Compose use top-level `mem_limit: 512m`, `cpus: 1.5`, `mem_reservation`. This is the #1 Compose gotcha: limits that work in staging Swarm do nothing in dev Compose. Encode both forms if you run both modes.

instruction: Which per-service knobs should every Compose service set?
output: Baseline: `init: true` (zombie reaping), `stop_signal` + `stop_grace_period`, `platform: linux/amd64` when images are arch-sensitive, per-service `logging: {driver, options}`, and `pull_policy`. These five lines prevent entire classes of dev/prod drift and belong in your compose template, not added after incidents.

instruction: When do Compose networks/volumes need external: true or a top-level name?
output: Mark shared infra `external: true` (created outside Compose: `dbdata:` volumes, `proxy:` networks) so `compose down` never deletes them. Set top-level `name: shop` to stop directory-renames from orphaning volumes/networks with new prefixed names. External + explicit names make Compose state survive refactors and CI checkout path changes.

instruction: pause/unpause vs stop, kill -s, and wait for CI scripts?
output: `docker pause` freezes via cgroup freezer (instant resume, keeps memory) — for temporary holds, not restarts. `docker kill -s HUP web` sends arbitrary signals for config reloads. In CI, `docker wait test-run` blocks until exit and prints the exit code — chain it: `run -d`, `wait`, then assert code 0 and `logs` on failure.

instruction: export vs save, and the create/start split?
output: `docker export` dumps a container's flattened filesystem (no history/layers); `docker save` preserves the image with layers for transfer. `docker import` turns a filesystem tarball into an image. Split setup from start with `docker create` (configure now) + `docker start` (run later) — useful when something else must exist first, like attaching networks pre-start.

instruction: How do I set up rootless Docker and what breaks?
output: Run `dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install` with proper subuid/subgid ranges; the daemon runs as your user with no root anywhere. Limitations: no `--privileged`, no host-network/mounts outside your namespace, overlay quirks on some filesystems, and ports <1024 need routing tricks. Choose rootless for single-user dev boxes, userns-remap for shared multi-user daemons.

instruction: Can I containerize Windows apps, and what are the catches?
output: Yes with Windows images (`mcr.microsoft.com/windows/nanoserver:ltsc2022` tiny, `servercore` fuller) and `SHELL ["powershell", "-Command"]` as default shell — but Windows containers run only on Windows hosts (no Linux mix), need matching host build for process isolation, and are far larger. Prefer Linux containers unless the app genuinely requires Windows APIs.

instruction: Podman, nerdctl, dockershim — do I need to care?
output: Podman runs daemonless + rootless with the same CLI (`alias docker=podman` mostly works; Compose via podman-compose or podman socket). nerdctl targets containerd directly. Kubernetes dropped dockershim — clusters use containerd/CRI-O, so `docker` commands on nodes are gone (use `crictl`). Your Dockerfiles and Compose skills transfer; only the runtime plumbing differs.

instruction: How do I migrate Compose workloads to Kubernetes?
output: Convert with `kompose convert -f compose.yml` for a first draft, then hand-fix probes, resources and ingress — generated manifests are a starting point, not production. Longer term, rewrite as Helm charts or Kustomize overlays with proper liveness/readiness, resource requests/limits and PDBs. Migrate stateless services first; databases move last with a tested backup/restore drill.

instruction: How do I gate images in CI with Trivy?
output: Scan and fail on fixable criticals: `trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed user/app:1.0`, upload SARIF to GitHub code scanning for tracking. Combine with hadolint (Dockerfile lint), tag pinning policy and weekly rebuild cadence. A gate nobody can bypass beats perfect coverage — make the pipeline, not developers, say no.

instruction: What is a Kubernetes Ingress?
output: An API object defining HTTP/HTTPS routing rules (host and path based) into Services, typically with TLS termination. It needs an ingress controller such as NGINX, Traefik or HAProxy to actually implement it. The newer Gateway API is a more expressive successor.

instruction: What causes ImagePullBackOff and ErrImagePull?
output: The node cannot pull the image. Causes: typo in image name or tag, tag doesn't exist, private registry without `imagePullSecrets`, registry rate limits or network and DNS problems from the node. `kubectl describe pod` shows the exact pull error in Events; test the pull manually with `crictl pull` on the node.

instruction: Why is my Pod stuck in Pending?
output: The scheduler can't place it. `kubectl describe pod` shows the reason: insufficient CPU/memory on nodes, unsatisfied nodeSelector/affinity, node taints without matching tolerations, an unbound PersistentVolumeClaim, or quota limits. Check capacity with `kubectl describe nodes` and `kubectl get pvc`.

instruction: What is a DaemonSet used for?
output: It runs one Pod on every node (or a selected subset), including nodes added later. Typical uses are log collectors (Fluent Bit), monitoring agents (node-exporter), CNI plugins and storage daemons.

instruction: Explain how to run Nginx in Docker serving a local folder.
output: `docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 -v $(pwd)/site:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro nginx:alpine`. Browse to http://localhost:8080. To use a custom config, mount it at /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf.

instruction: What do liveness, readiness and startup probes do?
output: Liveness probes detect a stuck container and make the kubelet restart it. Readiness probes decide whether a Pod should receive Service traffic; failing readiness removes it from endpoints without restarting. Startup probes give slow-starting apps time before liveness checks begin. Each can be httpGet, tcpSocket, exec or grpc, with settings like initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds and failureThreshold.
